plan: Sell all leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL, MUU) to zero for capital preservation.
Trim QQQI to 20% to reduce concentration and meet the single-name mandate.
Sell SMH due to its downtrend and to reduce overall tech concentration.
Increase SPY to 25% for more broad market exposure and stability.
Buy XLV at 5% to diversify into a top-scoring, non-tech sector.
conservative.read: This conservative plan aims for capital preservation with a target of ~1.5% per month. It significantly reduces leverage and concentration, prioritizing stability. Expect lower drawdowns but also more modest growth potential.

plan: Trim SOXL to 3%, SPAL to 1%, and MUU to 2% to reduce overall leveraged ETF exposure.
Trim QQQI to 20% to meet the single-name concentration mandate.
Reduce SMH to 5% to lower semiconductor concentration.
Buy XLV at 4% to add diversification with a strong scanner setup.
This plan balances risk and growth, keeping total adds within limits.
balanced.read: This balanced plan focuses on risk-first growth, targeting ~2.5% per month. It reduces leverage and concentration while maintaining exposure to quality tech and broad indices. Expect moderate drawdowns and growth.

moves.note: Add top scanner setup for growth

plan: Add to SOXL, SPAL, and MUU to 6% each, leaning into leveraged ETFs for aggressive growth.
Trim QQQI to 15% to free up capital for higher growth opportunities.
Increase SMH to 12% to concentrate in the semiconductor sector.
Buy XLV at 5% to add a high-scoring, diversified long setup.

aggressive.read: This aggressive plan aims for stretch growth, targeting ~4% per month. It significantly increases exposure to leveraged ETFs and concentrates in high-scoring setups. Be aware of higher potential drawdowns and the daily decay/rebalancing of leveraged ETFs.

plan: Sell all leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL, MUU) to zero for income focus.
Sell SMH and CRWD to reduce high-beta tech exposure.
Add QQQI to 30% to increase income-generating assets.
Add SPY to 30% for broad market exposure and stability.
This plan prioritizes steady monthly distributions and low drawdown.
income.read: This income plan aims to park cash for yield, targeting ~1% per month. It rotates into income and broad index ETFs, cutting high-beta names. While prioritizing low drawdown and reliable income, distributions are variable and NAV can still fall in a selloff.
